title: Surge containment allocator with KV priority decay
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: During mixed-tenancy burst events we observe KV cache bloat combined with activation spikes that erode GPU headroom and cause request-level latency SLO violations. Existing soft-watermark eviction and global preemption policies are reactive and either over-aggressive (dropping useful KVs) or too timid (allowing slow ramp to OOM/latency floods).

Goal: Build a surge-containment allocator that enforces a short-term memory fence when headroom falls below dynamic thresholds, plus a KV priority decay mechanism that preferentially ages low-utility KV shards instead of indiscriminate eviction. The allocator should integrate with continuous-batching so batching decisions are aware of transient headroom and can reduce batch depth proactively.

Approach:
- Telemetry: add a short-window headroom sensor (25–60s rolling) that emits percent-available for weights/KV/activations separately and combined. Use these signals for short-term policy decisions.
- Memory fence: when combined headroom < X% (configurable), enter surge-containment mode for N seconds: limit concurrent batches, cap per-request activation reservation, prevent batch coalescing that increases tail latency.
- KV priority decay: maintain a per-tenant decay score for KV entries based on last-use timestamp, model-compatibility score (exact match vs approx), token-prefix hit rate, and reuse velocity. Decay older/lower-score shards first and allow safe fallback to compressed on-host spill for lower-priority shards.
- Adaptive throttling: connect allocator output to continuous-batching controller to bias for smaller, lower-latency batches under surge. Provide a gradual ramp-down to avoid oscillation.
- Fallbacks: if eviction and throttling cannot restore headroom, gracefully fall back to model-variant routing (smaller quantized model) before OOM.

Deliverables: implementation in runtime allocator, new telemetry dashboard, e2e stress test harness, a guide for operators with tuning knobs and runbook entries.
acceptance_criteria: Headroom sensor telemetry available in metrics pipeline and visible in the GPU Budget dashboard
Surge-containment mode triggers when combined headroom < configured threshold and reduces concurrent batch depth by >= 30% during window
KV priority decay reduces eviction of high-reuse shards (measured via 90th percentile reuse retention) compared to LRU baseline
No increase in 95th percentile token-latency for normal steady-state traffic when feature is disabled via config
Playbook added: steps to tune thresholds and manual override; documented release notes
comments: 2026-03-02 — Maya Chen: Initial spike analysis attached (link) — saw correlated KV growth with mixed short queries from customer A. Proposed headroom sensor thresholds at 12%/8%/5% for warning/containment/critical.

2026-03-04 — Arjun Patel: Prototype memory fence integrated with batch controller. Short window test shows 35% reduction in concurrency during simulated surge. Need to quantify cost tradeoff for tail throughput.
2026-03-06 — Sofia Martinez (SRE): Observed that KV decay must be tenant-aware — high-priority tenants should have slower decay. Requested per-tenant policy knobs and audit logs for evictions.

2026-03-08 — Arjun Patel: Implemented KV decay scoring (last_use, prefix_hit_rate, model_match). Added on-host compressed spill path for decay tier. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
2026-03-10 — UX request from PM: Console needs a combined headroom view plus live state indicating which GPUs are in surge-containment. Added work item for console team (PM-1489).

2026-03-12 — Maya Chen: Runbook draft uploaded to Confluence (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GPU/Surge+Containment+Runbook). Scheduler still needs hysteresis tuning to avoid oscillation under periodic microbursts.
notes: Performance experiments show trade-offs: aggressive containment reduces tail latency but increases token cost for bursty tenants due to smaller batches; we'll expose knobs per-tenant and include a default conservative profile. Next steps: add A/B to production canary and monitor cost/perf delta for top-20 tenants.
